18438.content:
`BLI_Stack` is a generic stack in the [[Blender BLI API]] that stores fixed-size elements in linked chunks. Its public operations create and free a stack, push or pop values, inspect the top, clear or discard entries, count elements, and test whether the stack is empty.

Popping copies the last element to caller-provided storage and then discards that position without necessarily releasing the allocated memory. The [[Blender BLI Stack Chunk]] organization allows storage to be reused and avoids a separate allocation for every pushed item.

A `StackChunk` is a linked allocation unit used by [[Blender BLI Stack]]. The stack tracks a current chunk, a pool of free chunks, the current element index, element size, capacity per chunk, and optionally the total number of stored elements.

Chunking targets substantial blocks of memory and a minimum number of elements, reducing repeated allocator overhead. When values are removed, storage can remain available through the free-chunk list, making the container suitable for repeated push-and-pop workloads in the Blender codebase.

18465.heading: Blender Blend File Loading Pipeline
18465.content:
Factory loading starts at the [[Blender Core Entry Point]], reaches `WM_init()`, and then follows `wm_homefile_read()`, `BKE_blendfile_read_from_memory()`, and `BLO_read_from_memory()`. The loader first creates a [[Blender FileData Structure]], validates the header and DNA, and then parses blocks through a common internal path.

That shared path produces a [[Blender BlendFileData Structure]] whether bytes came from memory or storage. [[Blender LibBlock Linking]] assembles its records into a [[Blender Main Database]], after which [[Blender Context Main Assignment]] makes the new state active.

18492.content:
An armature is a structured collection of bones used to pose and deform an object. Each bone has a head and tail, and connected or parented bones form a controllable skeleton.

Skinning binds mesh vertices to the armature. Vertex groups assign weights that determine how strongly each bone influences each vertex, providing finer control than broad bone envelopes.

An armature object stores a hierarchy of bones used to pose and deform other objects. The armature provides the transformable control structure, while vertex groups and modifiers determine how a mesh follows those bones.

Keeping the rig separate from render geometry allows animation to be edited without rebuilding the surface. Export settings must preserve the needed hierarchy, deformed bones, and actions when the asset moves into a game engine.

Blender application handlers are functions registered to run around recurring events such as frame changes, scene updates, rendering, loading, or saving. They are stored in event-specific lists, so ordinary list operations can add, remove, clear, or inspect the callbacks.

The template's value is consistency. Repeated class fields and lifecycle functions make the script readable and provide known places for diagnostics, property creation, and cleanup. Registration makes an add-on's classes and properties available to Blender; unregistration removes them when the add-on is disabled or reloaded. Dependent classes should be registered in a logical order and unregistered in reverse order so that no component is removed while another still relies on it.

The source describes both explicit per-class calls and module-wide helpers available in Blender 2.78c. Its development template favors a clean slate before registering newly evaluated classes. Regardless of version-specific functions, reliable add-ons make activation repeatable, cleanup complete, and accidental duplicate registration visible.

18513.content:
An add-on can register properties on Blender scene or object types so that values become accessible through the current context and can be saved with the `.blend` file. Scene properties are useful for settings that apply to the current scene rather than to a temporary local variable.

Properties closely tied to one operator or panel can be created in that class's registration method, while broader settings can be created by the module's registration function. Unregistration should delete the same properties, preventing stale interface state from surviving after the add-on is removed.

A multi-file Blender add-on must distinguish its first package import from later development reloads. On first load, a sibling module is imported relative to the package; on reload, the already known module is explicitly refreshed so edits become part of the running add-on.

The source uses the presence of `bpy` in local names to select these paths and imports `bpy` afterward. The exact protocol reflects its Blender and Python version, but the broader issue persists: module caches can preserve old code unless the development lifecycle deliberately refreshes dependencies.

18519.content:
Filesystem development places an add-on directly in Blender's add-ons directory and edits it with an external text editor. The same package that appears in user preferences is therefore both the development artifact and the deployment structure.

This removes the risky conversion between scripts written in Blender's Text Editor and packages installed from disk. Single files, flat packages, and multilevel Python modules can all be valid structures. The appropriate depth depends on functional complexity and organization rather than line count alone.

18522.heading: Blender Add-On External Data
18522.content:
Blender add-ons can obtain predefined geometry from interchange files, embed raw data in Python, or construct forms algorithmically from primitives. The choice affects extensibility, readability, package size, and how naturally users can parameterize the result.

External files are a strong default when an asset is substantially fixed because artists and tools can replace them without editing code. Algorithmic construction is strongest when variation is the purpose of the add-on. Hardcoded mesh arrays can work, but they bind data tightly to implementation and make collaboration more difficult.

18525.content:
A distributable Blender add-on packages its main initialization file and dependent modules into a predictable directory, commonly delivered as a compressed archive that Blender can install. Metadata describes the package, and registration functions provide the entry points Blender invokes when users enable or disable it.

Distribution should not require recipients to edit development imports or remove diagnostic code. The source's early workflow performs those conversions manually, then its advanced workflow argues for developing directly in the add-on filesystem so the tested structure is already the deployed structure. Packaging is safest when development and installation exercise the same code paths.

18540.heading: Blazor

Blazor is Microsoft's framework for building interactive web interfaces with Razor markup and C#. In the 2019 source, it connects familiar ASP.NET-style component syntax to either server-side execution or an experimental client-side WebAssembly model.

A `.razor` component combines HTML, event bindings, and a C# code block. The framework tracks state changes and updates the displayed document, letting developers create a single-page interaction without writing the component behavior in JavaScript.

18546.title: Blackbody Radiation
18546.heading: Blackbody Radiation
18546.content: A blackbody is an ideal absorber and emitter whose thermal spectrum depends only on temperature. Classical theory predicted an unphysical ultraviolet divergence, while Planck reproduced the observed spectrum by quantizing oscillator energy in multiples of $hf$. Increasing temperature raises total emitted power and shifts the spectral peak to shorter wavelength.

18555.title: Bivariate Normal Distribution
18555.heading: Bivariate Normal Distribution
18555.content:
A bivariate normal distribution jointly describes two normally distributed variables through their two means, two standard deviations, and a correlation coefficient. Under this model, conditional expectations follow a line whose slope depends on the correlation and relative scales.

The compact five-parameter description explains why [[Pearson Correlation Coefficient|correlation]] is informative in this setting. When the joint shape is not approximately bivariate normal, the same coefficient may conceal nonlinear structure, outliers, or poor agreement.

18558.title: Bivariate Choropleth
18558.heading: Bivariate Choropleth
18558.content: A bivariate choropleth encodes two attributes within the same regional fill. The source combines hue for a categorical variable with transparency or lightness for a quantitative variable, producing a two-dimensional legend. The technique can reveal joint spatial patterns but quickly becomes difficult to decode, so category and value levels should be limited. Separate [[Small-Multiple Choropleth|small multiples]] may be preferable when either variable needs detailed reading.

18561.title: BITNET
18561.heading: BITNET
18561.content:
BITNET began in 1981 as a network connecting IBM mainframes at universities. It provided messaging, file transfer, and Listserv discussion groups to communities that often lacked access to ARPANET.

Connections with other networks eventually brought its users into the Internet. BITNET broadened network culture beyond technical and military research groups.

Bitmap font rendering converts text glyphs into textured images that can be drawn with the game renderer. A font library can rasterize a requested string at a chosen size, producing a texture for later interface display.

Repeated text should be cached because rasterization and texture creation are more expensive than drawing an existing result. Dynamic or frequently changing text may instead use a [[Font Texture Atlas]].

18567.title: Bisection Method
18567.heading: Bisection Method
18567.content:
The bisection method finds a root of a continuous function on an interval whose endpoints have opposite signs. It repeatedly halves the interval and keeps the half that still brackets a sign change.

The method converges reliably under its assumptions and has a predictable error bound based on interval width. Its convergence is slower than derivative-based methods but does not require a derivative.

BIRCH incrementally inserts observations into a height-balanced clustering-feature tree. Leaf entries summarize compact subclusters, and a threshold controls whether a new point can be absorbed or requires a new entry.

A single scan can compress a large dataset into memory before a global clusterer is applied to leaf summaries. Input order and the absorption threshold affect the tree, and non-spherical structures may be poorly represented by compact statistics.

18573.title: BIRCH Clustering
18573.heading: BIRCH Clustering
18573.content:
BIRCH is a hybrid method for large numerical databases that first compresses observations into a height-balanced cluster-feature tree and then applies a global partitioning method to the leaf summaries.

The method can build its in-memory representation in one scan and restart with a larger diameter threshold when the tree is too large. It remains sensitive to input order and favors roughly spherical groups of similar size.

18576.heading: Biot-Savart Law
18576.content:
The Biot-Savart law gives the magnetic field contribution from a current element:

$$dB=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I\,d\ell\times\hat r}{r^2}.$$

Integrating along the conductor produces the total field. The cross product fixes direction through the right-hand rule, while geometry determines how contributions reinforce or cancel.

18579.title: Biometric Authentication
18579.heading: Biometric Authentication
18579.content:
Biometric authentication uses a measured physical or behavioral characteristic as evidence of identity. Fingerprints, facial features, voice, and other traits belong to the inherent category in [[Authentication Factor Categories]].

Biometric matching is probabilistic rather than a perfect equality test, so systems must manage false acceptance and rejection. Because a biometric characteristic is difficult to replace after exposure, it is often stronger as one factor in [[Multi-Factor Authentication]] than as a standalone secret.

18582.title: Biomanufacturing Cost
18582.heading: Biomanufacturing Cost
18582.content:
Biomanufacturing cost includes cells, media, scaffolds, equipment, facilities, labor, quality control, failed batches, storage, and transport. A successful proof of concept may be unaffordable because it uses small bespoke batches and research-grade materials.

Automation and purchasing scale can lower cost, but sterility and biological quality requirements prevent every industrial shortcut used with passive materials.

Biological material responsiveness is the ability of living material to sense conditions and change its form or function. Muscle strengthens with repeated loading, skin initiates repair after injury, and cells alter behavior in response to chemical, electrical, and mechanical signals.

This adaptiveness motivates biofabrication but also makes final behavior less fixed than that of an ordinary manufactured part.

18597.heading: Biological Material Ownership
18597.content:
Biological material ownership concerns control and benefit when donated cells are expanded, modified, patented, or incorporated into valuable products. The physical sample, derived cell line, genetic information, manufacturing process, and finished construct may involve different claims.

Governance should distinguish legal possession from continuing obligations of consent, privacy, attribution, access, and benefit sharing.

18600.title: Biological Autonomy
18600.heading: Biological Autonomy
18600.content:
Biological autonomy is a system's ability to maintain and organize its own continued operation rather than relying on an external operator for every essential condition. Metabolism alone is insufficient if an incubator, media supply, and fabricated scaffold perform the broader self-maintenance.

Autonomy exists by degree, making it useful for distinguishing living cells from an independently living biofabricated organism.

18603.title: Biological Actuator
18603.heading: Biological Actuator
18603.content:
A biological actuator converts cellular energy into mechanical force and motion. Engineered muscle is attractive because it produces high force for its volume and responds to electrical, neural, chemical, or optical stimulation.

Unlike an electric motor, living muscle needs nutrients and compatible surroundings but can remodel itself in response to loading and damage.

18606.title: Biohybrid Swimmer
18606.heading: Biohybrid Swimmer
18606.content:
A biohybrid swimmer converts tissue contraction into thrust through a flexible body, fin, or tail. Cardiac cells provide rhythmic bending, while body shape determines how those deformations push against the surrounding liquid.

Adding a second tail or coordinating waves across a fin can greatly change speed and steering without changing the underlying cell type.

18609.title: Biohybrid Robot
18609.heading: Biohybrid Robot
18609.content:
A biohybrid robot uses living tissue to contribute to sensing, control, or response while operating as an engineered machine. Current examples commonly attach muscle to flexible skeletons so contraction creates movement.

The robot's material can mature, fatigue, strengthen, or heal, making biological state and environmental support part of its control problem.

18612.heading: Biohybrid Robot Exercise Adaptation
18612.content:
Biohybrid robot exercise adaptation is the increase in engineered muscle performance after repeated stimulation. Training signals impose recurring contraction and loading, prompting living tissue to reorganize and generate greater force.

The response distinguishes a biological actuator from a fixed synthetic one, while also making prior use, recovery, fatigue, and culture conditions part of device calibration.

18615.title: Biohybrid Machine
18615.heading: Biohybrid Machine
18615.content:
A biohybrid machine combines living biological components with synthetic structures, electronics, or materials to perform a designed function. The biological part may provide actuation, sensing, adaptation, or processing that is difficult to reproduce synthetically.

Its operation depends on both mechanical interfaces and life-support conditions, so maintenance of the cells is part of maintaining the machine.

18618.title: Biohybrid Gripper
18618.heading: Biohybrid Gripper
18618.content:
A biohybrid gripper uses contractile tissue to bring flexible jaws or edges together around an object. Sustained high-frequency stimulation can keep muscle contracted and maintain the grip.

Soft living actuation may suit delicate samples, but controlled release, force calibration, fatigue, sterility, and the device's dependence on culture conditions limit practical deployment.

A biofabrication supply chain moves cell banks, media ingredients, scaffolds, equipment, living intermediates, and finished products among specialized facilities. Temperature, sterility, time, provenance, and biological viability impose constraints beyond ordinary manufactured goods.

Distributed production can shorten final transport but requires standardized inputs, skilled operators, monitoring, and reliable cold or controlled-environment logistics.

Biofabrication stakeholder governance brings researchers, clinicians, patients, donors, consumers, workers, policy makers, ethicists, journalists, and the public into decisions about research and deployment. Each group sees different risks, needs, and distributions of benefit.

Expert self-governance can establish technical safeguards, but durable legitimacy requires participation from people affected outside the laboratory.

18627.heading: Biofabrication Scale-Up
18627.content:
Biofabrication scale-up expands a laboratory process to produce far greater quantities with controlled cost and quality. Larger bioreactors, automated handling, reliable cell banks, process monitoring, and contamination control must replace repeated manual fabrication.

Biological variability and transport limits mean that simply enlarging every vessel can change cell behavior, so scale often requires redesign rather than multiplication.

A biofabrication regulatory pathway defines the evidence, manufacturing controls, classification, and oversight required before a living-cell product reaches patients or consumers. Existing rules may have been designed for human implants, drugs, food, or animal tissue rather than the new combination.

Regulation must establish identity, origin, safety, consistency, labeling, traceability, and the consequences of process changes.

18633.title: Biofabrication Literacy
18633.heading: Biofabrication Literacy
18633.content:
Biofabrication literacy is the practical understanding needed to evaluate how living-cell technologies are made, what they can and cannot do, and which economic, environmental, and ethical choices accompany them. It is relevant to citizens and consumers as well as specialists.

Shared vocabulary enables meaningful public participation, adaptive education, and governance before products and labor markets have already changed.

Biofabrication injection molding fills a shaped cavity with cells suspended in a hydrogel precursor and solidifies the mixture under cell-compatible conditions. It rapidly produces millimeter- or centimeter-scale parts with the mold's external geometry.

The approach is robust but usually creates homogeneous material and offers limited control over internal microscale architecture or multiple materials.

18639.heading: Biofabrication Ethics Vignette
18639.content:
A biofabrication ethics vignette is a concrete imagined scenario used to examine the values and uncertainties around a possible technology. A case such as unusually strong engineered muscle makes downstream questions about enhancement, access, safety, and responsibility discussable.

Vignettes do not predict the future; they expose assumptions and help participants locate boundaries before a real decision becomes urgent.

18642.heading: Biofabrication Ethical Tradeoff
18642.content:
A biofabrication ethical tradeoff compares competing benefits and harms when no option satisfies every value. A more complex tissue model may improve medical prediction while increasing moral concern; customization may improve care while raising cost and unequal access.

Making the tradeoff explicit identifies whose benefits count, who bears risk, what uncertainty remains, and which alternatives were excluded.

18645.title: Biocompatible Material
18645.heading: Biocompatible Material
18645.content:
A biocompatible material performs its intended role without producing unacceptable harm to the contacting cells or tissue. Compatibility depends on chemistry, degradation products, stiffness, surface behavior, dose, duration, and the biological setting.

For biofabrication, the material must also tolerate manufacturing conditions that preserve cell viability and function.

18648.heading: Biochemical Differentiation Cue
18648.content:
A biochemical differentiation cue is a soluble or matrix-bound signal that guides an immature cell toward a specialized lineage. Growth factors, hormones, and medium composition can activate developmental pathways associated with cartilage, muscle, bone, or other tissues.

The identity, concentration, timing, and combination of cues determine both efficiency and the maturity of the resulting cells.

18651.title: Binomial
18651.heading: Binomial
18651.content:
A binomial is a [[Polynomial]] with two terms, such as (x+3) or (a^2-b^2). The terms are joined by addition or subtraction at the outermost level.

Products of binomials can be expanded by distributing every term, sometimes remembered through the [[FOIL Method]]. Particular binomial structures generate important identities: conjugates (a+b) and (a-b) produce a difference of squares, while cubed binomials produce four-term expansions. Binomials also commonly appear as factors of quadratic polynomials.

18654.title: Binomial Logistic Model
18654.heading: Binomial Logistic Model
18654.content:
A binomial logistic model is a generalized linear model whose outcome follows a binomial structure and whose link function maps event probability to log odds. In R, specifying the binomial family tells the fitting routine to use this model rather than ordinary linear regression.

The outcome coding determines which state is modeled as the event. Analysts must verify the 0/1 representation and reference levels before interpreting the coefficient signs or exponentiating them into odds ratios.

18657.title: Binomial Distribution
18657.heading: Binomial Distribution
18657.content:
The binomial distribution gives the probability of observing a specified number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials when every trial has the same success probability. Its parameters are the trial count and the per-trial probability.

It models biological counts such as variant-supporting reads when the trials and probability assumptions are appropriate. With many trials and a moderate expected count it approaches a normal shape, while rare events motivate a [[Rare Event Poisson Approximation]].

18660.title: Bind Pose
18660.heading: Bind Pose
18660.content:
The bind pose is the reference pose in which a mesh is attached to its [[Skeleton Hierarchy]]. Each bone has a local bind transform and a derived global bind transform in object space.

Vertex positions are authored in this common object-space pose. The [[Inverse Bind Pose Matrix]] later moves each position into the coordinate space of a contributing bone before its animated transform is applied.

18663.title: Binary Search
18663.heading: Binary Search
18663.content:
Binary search locates a target in ordered data by examining the middle item. A match ends the search; a smaller or larger middle value proves that one half cannot contain the target, so the algorithm continues only in the other half.

Repeated halving gives [[Logarithmic Time Complexity]], $O(\log n)$, and makes extremely large ordered collections searchable with few probes. The algorithm also reports failure when its [[Search Space]] becomes empty. Implementations must calculate the midpoint without causing [[Integer Overflow]].

18666.title: Binary Representation in Hardware
18666.heading: Binary Representation in Hardware
18666.content:
Early computer engineers chose binary codes because two-state circuits and storage devices were simpler and more reliable than components that had to distinguish many voltage levels. Groups of bits could represent numbers, instructions, text, images, and other discrete information.

Binary digits are abstractions over physical states such as voltages, magnetic orientations, or stored charge. Syntax rules distinguish valid code patterns, even though the machine does not understand what the patterns mean.

18669.title: Binary Relation
18669.heading: Binary Relation
18669.content:
A binary relation from A to B is a [[Subset]] of the [[Cartesian Product]] A × B. Writing a R b means that the ordered pair (a, b) belongs to the relation R.

A relation on one set can be reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric, or transitive. Particular combinations define partial orders and equivalence relations, while [[Transitive Closure]] extends a relation to capture reachability through one or more steps.

18672.title: Binary Operation
18672.heading: Binary Operation
18672.content:
A binary operation on a set assigns an element of the same set to every ordered pair of its elements. Closure is built into this definition, while associativity, commutativity, identities, and inverses are separate properties.

A group is obtained when an associative operation has an identity and an inverse for every element.

18675.title: Binary Outcome Variable
18675.heading: Binary Outcome Variable
18675.content:
A binary outcome variable encodes whether an event or condition is present, usually with 1 for the event and 0 for its absence. This representation is used directly by [[Logistic Regression]] and can also serve as the event indicator in time-to-event analysis.

Special responses such as refused, uncertain, or missing should not be silently converted into absence. The source categories must first be validated, then recoded so every retained observation has an unambiguous outcome state.

18678.title: Binary Mesh File
18678.heading: Binary Mesh File
18678.content:
A binary mesh file stores vertex, index, and related mesh data in a compact byte layout designed for direct runtime loading. It avoids the parsing and character-conversion cost of a text representation and typically occupies less disk space.

The efficiency comes from a stricter contract. Writer and reader must agree on the [[Binary File Header]], field order, numeric sizes, counts, and the exact vertex format expected by the renderer.

18681.heading: Binary Game Data
18681.content:
Binary game data stores values in a compact machine-oriented representation. It is generally smaller and faster to load than [[Text-Based Game Data]] because the runtime performs less parsing and numeric conversion.

The format is difficult to inspect or merge directly and must manage version, byte order, and structural compatibility. A common pipeline authors readable source data and converts it into a validated binary form for distribution.

18684.title: Binary File Header
18684.heading: Binary File Header
18684.content:
A binary file header places identifying and structural metadata before a binary payload. A mesh header can record a signature, version, vertex format, vertex count, index count, and offsets or sizes needed to interpret following bytes.

Validation prevents the loader from treating an unrelated, truncated, or incompatible file as trusted geometry. Because binary data is not self-describing, the header carries the minimum information required to enforce the format contract.

18687.title: Bill Co-Sponsorship Network
18687.heading: Bill Co-Sponsorship Network
18687.content:
A bill co-sponsorship network links legislators who jointly present or support proposed legislation. Legislators are nodes, and shared sponsorship supplies an observable relationship of collaboration or support.

The network can be built for a whole term or separated into legislative sessions. Its centrality and community patterns may reveal cohesion, cross-party relationships, splitting, and switching, while remaining an imperfect proxy for private motives.
